authors: C. W. Blount, L. C. Price, L. M. Wenger, M. Tarullo
journal: U.S. DOE final report DOE/ET/12145-1 (OSTI), 'Solubility of methane in water under natural conditions: a laboratory study'
experimental_method: Hydrothermal solution equipment (rocked pressure vessel holding a teflon sample cell, after Dickson, Blount and Tunell 1963) equilibrated with 99.99% CH4 (or CH4+CO2 / CH4+C2H6 mixtures) for up to two days; liquid samples withdrawn above the run pressure into pre-weighed evacuated flasks, exsolved gas measured by pressure (ideal gas law, with compression correction Pc) and, for mixtures, composition by gas chromatography.
uncertainties_stated: Experimental results 'nearly +/-7% of the value' (report p.13); T +/-4 F gives +/-1%; P +/-60 psi gives about +/-2%; NaCl concentration +/-0.1% gives about +/-0.5% (p.14); combined T/P/NaCl effect < +/-2.5%; uncertainty unlikely below +/-6%. Equipment section (p.7) states T controlled and measured to +/-3 F and P measured to +/-45 psi (Heise Bourdon gauge); flask gas pressure +/-0.05 psi. Duplicate/triplicate samples usually within +/-5% of their mean (p.11). Low-P/low-T data (Table A-2): usually +/-10 to +/-25 percent of the mean, std. dev. of repeats 0.2-0.5 SCF/Bbl (p.33).
quality_remarks: Samples analysed as moles CH4 per kg of solution and converted to SCF/Bbl (standard cubic feet at 25 C and 1 atm per 42-gallon barrel of brine) 'using appropriate conversion factors' that are not given (p.13, p.15). The 10.0 percent NaCl runs at 401 and 464 F (all pressures) were deleted as erroneous (lower than 15 percent NaCl values; suspected thermocouple malfunction) before Table A-1 was compiled, together with occasional other points far off linear plots; 670 points remain (p.15). Erratic results (gas bubbles in the exit tube, leaks) were discarded and are not in the report (p.13). Values in the earlier conference paper (Blount et al. 1979, 4th Geopressured-Geothermal Conference) were 5-20% high because the solution-compression correction Pc was omitted; recalculated values appeared in Price et al. 1981 (p.13; conclusions p.66). The teflon cell was permeable to CH4, CO2 and C2H6 and slightly to water, so NaCl concentration drifted (diluted) and was re-measured and reloaded when it dropped about 0.5 wt% (p.9, p.12); per-row salinities in Tables A-2 to A-4 reflect this. In the CO2 runs a constant CO2 content could not be held; the gas phase was much poorer in CO2 than the dissolved gas (p.42). Ethane runs had GC reproducibility problems (p.51). Table A-2: text says 129 samples at 34 conditions at 77/122/160 F and 52/107/167 g/L; table prints 128 rows, T 74-161 F plus a 212 F block, salinities 46-166 g/L. Table A-3: 84 rows / 27 conditions as stated; four rows disagree with Total x (1 - %CO2) and with the printed averages (9-1 total 51.1, probably 59.1; 17-1 CH4 43.2, probably 42.2; 21-1 and 21-2 CH4 45.2, implied 48.1 and 46.5); kept as printed. Table A-4: sample 19 CH4 34.5 vs implied 36.3, kept. Temperature scale not stated anywhere. Pressures in Table A-2 are psi absolute (footnote); Tables A-3/A-4 say only psi. Table A-1: rows 283-284 print 271.0 F inside a 277 F run (both passes read 271.0; probably a typing slip in the report, kept as printed). Exact repeats at the same T, P and salinity differ by up to about 12-15% (e.g. rows 365/366: 80.9 vs 91.5; 661/662: 52.7 vs 59.7), confirmed on the page image: scatter in the data, consistent with the stated +/-7%. Salinity drifts within runs because sampling depleted the cell and NaCl solution was re-injected. The text calls the analysed values averaged, but Table A-1 is titled and described as raw data; its rows are individual samples.

A-4: CH4 = Total x (1 - %C2H6/100) within 0.07 for 25 of 26 rows (exception sample 19).
